# On the hull-full upgrade screen show current upgrades

**Headline:** Add a permanent-only "currently owned upgrades/weapons" panel to the top-left of the hold-full choice overlay (`MineralChoiceScene`), derived from the run's permanent weapon and power-up levels so a temporary field pickup can never appear in it or inflate a displayed level.

## Original request (verbatim)

> When the player is offered a hull full upgrade they are given a list of three items, ones that are new are labelled, ones that are upgrades show the upgrade parameters. We also need to list (in the top left) the currently owned upgrades/weapons. This list should not include temporary, only permanent upgrades. If they show a level they should show only the permanent level not any temporary level upgrades.

> **Terminology:** the request says "hull full"; the shipped feature is the **hold-full choice** overlay (`MineralChoiceScene`, GDD §4.4.1), opened when the mineral hold fills. This brief treats "hull-full" as "hold-full", consistent with AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR and AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF.

## Problem statement

The hold-full choice now shows each offered item's name, a one-line description and (for levelled offers) a level-accurate change summary, plus a `★ New` badge for items the player does not own (AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR, AH-0MV2N2591007UGPD, AH-0MVL9P2SF009QFON). What the screen still hides is the **other half of the picture**: the build the player already has. A player offered "Spread Shot Lv.3" cannot see whether they own Rapid Fire Lv.4 or a Shield, so a levelled choice is made blind. The overlay is also the only moment where gameplay is paused and a permanent decision is taken, so it is the natural place to show the current permanent loadout.

## Users

- **Player (informed build choice):** "As a player, when the hold fills, I want to see everything I already own permanently — weapons and power-ups, with their permanent levels — so I can judge whether a new offer fits my build."
- **Player (no mental arithmetic):** "As a player, I don't want my displayed level to include a 10-second field pickup I happened to catch, because the permanent level is what the offer is priced against."
- **Designer/tuner:** "As a designer, I want the list derived from the same permanent-only snapshots the choice pool already uses, so the panel can never disagree with what is offered."

### Example user stories

- As a player with `Spread Shot Lv.2`, `Rapid Fire Lv.1` and `Shield Lv.3` permanently owned, I see those three listed top-left when the hold fills.
- As a player who caught a field `Spread Shot` five seconds ago (temporary stack only, no permanent grant), the panel does **not** list Spread Shot, and if I own `Rapid Fire Lv.1` the panel shows `Lv.1`, not `Lv.2`.
- As a player opening the very first hold-full choice of a run, the panel tells me plainly that I own nothing permanent yet.

## Acceptance Criteria

> The three presentation decisions were confirmed by the producer during intake (Q1 = A, Q2 = A, Q3 = A; see the Appendix).

- **AC1 — Owned permanent items are listed.** The hold-full overlay renders, in the top-left of the screen, every item the player owns **permanently** this run — permanent **weapons and power-ups** — as one row per item. The permanent `cannon` is excluded (it is the base weapon, never a permanent reward) and so is the `reset` utility.
- **AC2 — Permanent only.** Temporary (field-pickup) upgrades never appear in the panel, and a displayed level is the item's **permanent level only** (`getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()`), never `permanent + temporary`. A field-only item is absent from the panel and still offered as `★ New`.
- **AC3 — Single source of truth.** The panel's item names come from the shared choice/catalogue naming (`toChoiceOption(id).name` in `src/powerups/choice.ts`, itself backed by `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` / `WEAPON_NAMES`); no second name table or duplicated level arithmetic is introduced in the scene.
- **AC4 — Level display.** Every row always shows the item's permanent level as `Lv.N`, including `Lv.1` (e.g. `Spread Shot Lv.2`, `Shield Lv.3`, `Rapid Fire Lv.1`), matching the offer labels on the same screen so a level-1 item and a levelled item are unambiguously distinguishable.
- **AC5 — Presentation & empty state.** The panel is a **single flat list** under the heading `YOUR UPGRADES`, rendered top-left (weapons first, then power-ups, catalogue order within each kind, so the order is deterministic). When the player owns nothing permanently, the heading reads `YOUR UPGRADES — none yet` rather than an empty/blank region. The panel must not collide with the centred option column (3 options, `CHOICE_FIRST_ROW_Y`…`+ pitch × 2`) at the shipped game resolution.
- **AC6 — Gym↔game parity.** Every launcher that opens the hold-full choice (`PlayScene.openMineralChoice`, `GymFormationScene.openMineralChoice`, `GymWeaponLeveling.openMineralChoice`, `GymPowerUpLeveling.openMineralChoice`) supplies the same permanent snapshots it already passes to the strategy context, so the panel behaves identically in the game and every gym; no divergent copy.
- **AC7 — Teardown & lifecycle.** The panel is destroyed with the rest of the choice UI when a selection starts the 3-2-1 countdown, and is rebuilt from current state the next time the overlay opens (no stale carry-over between hold-full events).
- **AC8 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests cover the pure owned-loadout builder (permanent-only filtering, cannon/`reset` exclusion, deterministic ordering, `Lv.N` labels, empty case) and scene tests cover the rendered rows, the empty state, the teardown, and that a temporary-only weapon/power-up never appears and never raises a displayed level. Every test asserts a meaningful behaviour (TDD preferred).
- **AC9 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README (where the overlay is described) and GDD §4.4.1 (hold-full choice presentation).
- **AC10 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.)

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** behaviour lives once — a pure builder consumed through the launcher payload, rendered by the single shared `MineralChoiceScene`; the duplicate-body guard and gym-parity docs assertion must stay green.
- **Backward compatibility:** the overlay's `init` payload gains an **optional** field; isolated scene tests that launch it with `options` only must keep working (absence → panel omitted or empty state, decided by the implementation and covered by a test).
- **No live mutation:** the panel reflects the permanent snapshots captured at launch; it need not update while the overlay is open (the choice is applied after the countdown, at which point the overlay closes).
- **Do not change the offered options, their order, the change summaries, the `★ New` badge, or the 3-offer mechanism** — this item is additive presentation.
- **Keep the existing accessors intact:** `getOptionLabels()`, `getDetailLines()`, `getDescriptionLines()` assertions must not break; add a new accessor for the panel rows.
- **Bounded list:** the six-slot permanent cap (AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF, `src/powerups/slots.ts`) bounds the list to ≤ 6 kinds plus any `availableWhenSlotsFull` exemptions, so no scrolling/paging design is required.
- **Run-scoped only:** no leaderboard or persistence impact.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — modal overlay: opaque backdrop, `HOLD FULL — CHOOSE A POWER-UP` heading at `y = 120`, one centred option block every `CHOICE_ROW_PITCH = 84` px from `CHOICE_FIRST_ROW_Y = 200` (name → description → change summary/`★ New`); `getOptionLabels()` / `getDetailLines()` / `getDescriptionLines()`; `_teardownChoiceUi()` destroys backdrop, heading, controls, detail/description lines and the keydown listener when the countdown starts.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `openMineralChoice()` — already computes `weaponLevels: player.getWeaponLevels()` and `powerUpLevels: player.getPowerUpLevels()` for the strategy context, but passes only `options`, `fireSchedule`, demo auto-select params and `onSelect` to `scene.launch('MineralChoiceScene', …)`.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — same pattern (compute the two snapshots, pass options + `fireSchedule` + `onSelect`).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `openMiniBossReward()` — also launches `MineralChoiceScene`, with `buildUpgradeOptions({ weaponLevels, powerUpLevels })`; **no** owned panel supplied today (see Risks).
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `ChoiceOption`, `toChoiceOption(id)` (name + description from the shared catalogues), `WEAPON_NAMES`, `buildLevelUpOption`, `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions`.
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — `resolveSlotState(powerUpLevels, weaponLevels)` → `{ used, free, isFull, ownedIds }`; already filters the permanent `cannon` and derives occupancy from the two **permanent-only** snapshots.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `getWeaponLevels()` (permanent weapon grants only) and `getPowerUpLevels()` → `PowerUpLevelStore.getLevels()` (permanent power-up grants only).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — existing owned-item row label convention `"<Name> Lvl <N>"` for the in-run HUD rows.
- GDD §4.4.1 documents the hold-full choice overlay, its option copy and the change-summary/`★ New` contract; its **Permanent pick** bullet names only `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene` and `GymWeaponLeveling` as launchers.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — the hold-full launcher parity guard ("every launcher passes the common overlay payload", `HOLDFULL_LAUNCHERS`) lists only `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`; `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` also launches the overlay but is **absent** from that list.
- `src/choiceDescriptionsDocs.test.ts` — the existing §4.4.1 docs guard (overlay option copy); `src/powerUpSlotsDocs.test.ts` holds the same `holdFullChoiceSection()` helper pattern.

## Desired change

1. **Pure owned-loadout builder (new module, e.g. `src/powerups/ownedLoadout.ts`)** — `buildOwnedLoadout(powerUpLevels, weaponLevels)` returning the permanent loadout as display rows (`{ id, kind, name, level, label }`), ordered deterministically (weapons first, then power-ups, catalogue order within each kind), each labelled `"<Name> Lv.<N>"`. Filters non-drop ids (`cannon`, `reset`) via the existing `isWeaponDrop` guard and names rows through `toChoiceOption(id).name`, so naming stays single-sourced.
2. **Overlay payload** — `MineralChoiceScene.init` accepts the built rows (optional); `create()` renders them top-left as the `YOUR UPGRADES` heading plus one `Lv.N` row per item (and the `YOUR UPGRADES — none yet` empty state), stored for teardown and exposed via a new test accessor (e.g. `getOwnedUpgradeLines()`); `_teardownChoiceUi()` destroys them.
3. **Launchers** — each hold-full launcher passes the rows built from the **same** `getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()` snapshots it already gathers for the strategy, so the panel and the offers can never disagree. `GymPowerUpLeveling` currently passes **only** `powerUpLevels` to the strategy context, so it adds a `this.player?.getWeaponLevels() ?? []` read for the panel rows (a read of the same permanent snapshot, not new state); its offer pool stays power-ups-only. See the Open Question below.
4. **Tests and documentation** — as per AC8/AC9: builder unit tests plus scene assertions for the panel rows, empty state, teardown and temporary-level exclusion; extend the **hold-full launcher parity guard** (add `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` to `HOLDFULL_LAUNCHERS` and assert every launcher passes the owned rows); add launcher-level assertions that each hold-full scene forwards the rows; update GDD §4.4.1 (panel, permanent-only rule, and the launcher list that omits `GymPowerUpLeveling`) and extend the §4.4.1 docs guard in `src/choiceDescriptionsDocs.test.ts` so the panel copy cannot silently drift.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/ownedLoadout.ts` *(new)* — pure permanent-loadout builder; filters non-drop ids, names via `toChoiceOption`, formats the level label.
- `src/powerups/ownedLoadout.test.ts` *(new)* — permanent-only filtering, ordering, labels, empty case, temporary-only exclusion.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — top-left panel rendering, empty state, teardown, `getOwnedUpgradeLines()`.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — panel rows/empty state/teardown/temporary-exclusion assertions.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — pass the built rows to the overlay launch payload.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend `HOLDFULL_LAUNCHERS` with `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` and assert every launcher passes the owned-loadout rows (AC6 · gym↔game parity).
- `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — launcher-level assertions that the overlay receives the built rows (AC6).
- `src/choiceDescriptionsDocs.test.ts` — extend the §4.4.1 docs guard with the `YOUR UPGRADES` panel and its permanent-only rule (AC9).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.1 — document the owned-permanents panel and its permanent-only rule; correct the launcher list in the **Permanent pick** bullet to include `GymPowerUpLeveling`.
- `README.md` — feature pointer if the overlay's capabilities are listed there.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR** — Show upgrade change summary and New badge in the hold-full choice list (completed): built the option `changeSummary` / `★ New` detail line this panel sits beside.
- **AH-0MV2N2591007UGPD** — Upgrade and weapon descriptions (completed): added the description line and the shared catalogue copy the panel reuses.
- **AH-0MVL9P2SF009QFON** — Upgrade text must reflect the actual upgrade (completed): level-accurate summaries from the permanent level.
- **AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF** — Limit the number of powerup slots (in progress): the six-slot permanent cap bounds this list to ≤ 6 kinds; `resolveSlotState` uses the same permanent-only snapshots.
- **AH-0MUX802450085VZZ / AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9 / AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K** — Permanent vs temporary split for weapons and power-ups, and the single `PowerUpLevelStore` the panel reads.
- **AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2** — Show level/wave progress as 'Level N of 5, Wave M of K' (completed): the existing top-left HUD readout, hidden behind the overlay's opaque backdrop.
- **AH-0MU7JTFY1006QA8I** — HUD lives label overlapped by active power-ups list (completed): precedent for owned-item list layout care.
- GDD §4.4.1 (hold-full choice), §4.4.2 (weapon leveling), §4.4.3 (power-up leveling).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep (medium):** "show current upgrades" can drift into redesigning the overlay. Mitigation: additive panel only; no change to offers, ordering, summaries or badges. Further presentation ideas become linked work items.
- **Mini-boss reward overlay (medium):** `openMiniBossReward()` reuses `MineralChoiceScene` but is not the "hull-full" screen. Default (recorded non-blocking during intake, no objection raised): the panel is supplied by the **hold-full** launchers only; adding it to the mini-boss reward is a separate, cheap follow-up if wanted.
- **Layout collision (low):** option descriptions are wide, centred text; a top-left panel must stay clear of them at the shipped resolution. Verified by a scene test asserting the panel's anchor and by manual gym check.
- **Temporary-level leakage (low):** `getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()` are already permanent-only, but the panel must not be tempted to read `getWeaponLevel()` / `getPowerUpLevel()` (effective levels). Guarded by a test that adds a temporary stack and asserts the displayed level is unchanged.
- **Name drift (low):** mitigated by resolving every row name through `toChoiceOption` rather than a new table.
- **Test coupling (low):** existing label/detail/description accessor assertions must keep passing — the panel is a separate set of game objects.
- **Assumption:** "hull full" = the hold-full mineral choice overlay (the only permanent-choice list), consistent with the sibling items.

## Open questions (plan review)

- **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking) — weapons panel in `GymPowerUpLeveling`.** That gym passes only `powerUpLevels` (no `weaponLevels`) to the choice strategy context, so AC1 ("every permanently-owned weapon **and** power-up") and AC6 ("the same permanent snapshots it already passes to the strategy context") disagree there. **Default recorded for implementation:** build the panel from `getWeaponLevels()` + `getPowerUpLevels()` in every launcher, including `GymPowerUpLeveling`, so the panel always states the run's true permanent loadout; that gym's offer pool stays power-ups-only and the panel does not change it. Directed to: producer (confirm or overrule the default) — it only matters if the panel must mirror a gym's disabled weapon offers instead of the run's actual loadout.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-28 — `plan` skill, auto-complete path** (pre-check: effort Small / risk Low). Six review stages run on the existing intake brief; changes kept conservative and additive: Existing state records the stale parity-guard launcher list and the existing §4.4.1 docs guard; Desired change steps 3–4 make the panel's snapshot source, the parity-guard extension and the docs-guard update explicit; Key Files gains the parity guard, the four launcher tests and the docs guard; one non-blocking Open Question records the `GymPowerUpLeveling` weapon-snapshot default. No acceptance criteria changed; no children created (one small vertical slice, no phasing needed).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Recorded during intake for AH-0MVCRKAPL000L68Y (operator = Producer). Research performed before asking: read `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts`, `src/powerups/choice.ts`, `src/powerups/slots.ts`, `src/entities/Player.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, `src/ui/HUD.ts`, the four hold-full launchers, GDD §4.4.1–§4.4.3, and worklog items AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR, AH-0MV2N2591007UGPD, AH-0MVL9P2SF009QFON, AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF. All three questions were asked together (one round, multiple-choice with a stated recommendation) and answered in one reply.

- **Q1 — Content scope: which owned items appear in the top-left list?**
  - A: Every permanently-owned power-up **and** weapon drop (the permanent cannon excluded, field-only/temporary items excluded). — **Recommended:** simplest reading of the request, and matches the shared six-slot loadout that the choice pool already prices.
  - B: Weapons only.
  - C: Power-ups only.
  - **Answer (Producer, interactive reply):** **A** — every permanently-owned power-up and weapon drop; the cannon and field-only/temporary items are excluded.
  - **Research:** `Player.getWeaponLevels()` and `PowerUpLevelStore.getLevels()` both return permanent grants only; `resolveSlotState()` already treats power-ups and weapon drops as one shared loadout, so option A is a single flat list of at most six kinds plus slot-cap exemptions.

- **Q2 — Level format: how is the permanent level shown per row?**
  - A: Always show `Lv.N` on every row, including `Lv.1`. — **Recommended:** unambiguous and consistent with the adjacent offer labels (`"1.  Spread Shot Lv.3"`).
  - B: Show the level only when N ≥ 2 (`Spread Shot` alone at level 1).
  - C: Use the HUD's existing convention `Lvl N` (e.g. `Spread Shot Lvl 2`).
  - **Answer (Producer, interactive reply):** **A** — always show `Lv.N`, including `Lv.1`.
  - **Research:** the choice option names use `Lv.N` (`buildLevelUpOption`); the in-run HUD rows use `"<Name> Lvl <N>"` (`src/ui/HUD.ts`). Both conventions already ship, so either was defensible; the request only fixes *which* level (permanent) is shown, not the formatting.

- **Q3 — Presentation: heading and layout of the panel?**
  - A: One flat list under the heading `YOUR UPGRADES`, rows like `Spread Shot Lv.2`, and `YOUR UPGRADES — none yet` when nothing is permanently owned. — **Recommended:** minimum code that satisfies the request, and the names are self-explanatory.
  - B: Two grouped sections under the heading (`WEAPONS`, then `POWER-UPS`).
  - C: Flat list with slot usage in the heading (`YOUR UPGRADES 4/6`), tying the list to the six-slot cap (AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF).
  - **Answer (Producer, interactive reply):** **A** — one flat list under `YOUR UPGRADES`, with the `YOUR UPGRADES — none yet` empty state.
  - **Research:** the panel has the full top-left quadrant free (options occupy `y ≈ 200–420`, centred), and the six-slot cap bounds the list to ≤ 6 kinds, so all three options fit without scrolling. The empty state matters because the first hold-full of a run always occurs with zero permanent upgrades.

- **Non-blocking note — mini-boss reward overlay:** flagged that `openMiniBossReward()` reuses `MineralChoiceScene`; proposed default is hold-full launchers only. No objection recorded — implemented as the default (see Risks & assumptions).

- **Assumption — "hull full":** interpreted as the **hold-full mineral choice** overlay (the only permanent-choice list), consistent with AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR and AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF. No objection raised.
- **Assumption — no live refresh:** the panel reflects the state captured when the overlay opens; the overlay closes on selection, so no mid-overlay updates are required.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV** – Feature: Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling (completed)
- **AH-0MV70Y2XY005J2HI** – Hold-full overlay: fade the thruster/engine hum out while paused (completed)
- **AH-0MUX9T7C7003CBQP** – F3: Weapon temporary/permanent split (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muu1goau007rfvr, 0muv5clvo002zhs9, 0muv5clw6005vf7k, 0mux802450085vzz, 0mv2n2591007ugpd (+450 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0muv5clvo002zhs9, 0muv5clw6005vf7k, 0mv2n2591007ugpd, 0mvl9p2sf009qfon, absent (+442 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+386 more)

# evaluate.mjs --tune: fail fast on unwritable --out and survive hard kill without dirty CSV

## Summary
During the 2026-10-21 end-to-end tune-loop verification (AH-0MVBNLM2V008XC8T), the negative-probe command

  node scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune --set enemy-configs.csv boss.health=7 --games 2 --ticks 200 --out /proc/nope/x

hung for 166.6 minutes inside a single Pi bash call before being killed (exit 137 / SIGKILL) — the largest
single tool call of the day (2.8 h of ~11.8 h active agent time). Instead of failing fast on the unwritable
output path, the CLI runs both sweeps first and validates the output directory only at write time. A hard
kill also means the in-memory CSV restore in the finally block cannot run: the session log shows the CSV
dirty (M src/data/enemy-configs.csv, changed md5) immediately after the kill (clean now, restored by later
session activity). Root cause to confirm during implementation; hypotheses: (a) output-dir validation
happens only after the sweeps, (b) no internal watchdog/timeout on the sweep, (c) SIGKILL (OOM/timeout)
skips the finally-based restore, (d) the pipe to tail can mask the true exit.

## User stories
- As a developer running tune-loop verification I want --tune to validate --out (and the CSV path) up-front
  so an invalid path fails in seconds, not hours.
- As a developer I want the tune/edit cycle crash-safe so even a hard kill never leaves the balance CSV
  edited in the worktree.

## Suggested approach
1. Validate options.outputDir and src/data/<tuneFile> before booting the SSR core or running any batch:
   a quick mkdir/writeability probe with a clear message and non-zero exit (ideally < 2 s).
2. Make edit/restore crash-safe: persist a small journal (target path + original bytes) beside the CSV
   before editing; restore/reconcile from the journal on next invocation (and document a manual repair
   path); do not rely solely on an in-memory finally.
3. Add a bounded-runtime watchdog or per-phase progress output for the sweep so an abnormal run cannot
   stall silently for hours; 2x200-tick games should take minutes, not hours.
4. Confirm the root cause with a repro before fixing (see hypotheses above); verify the observed exit code
   and CSV state in the repro.

## Acceptance criteria
1. The repro command above fails fast (< 2 s) with a clear "output directory not writable" diagnostic and
   a non-zero exit; demonstrated before and after the fix.
2. --tune with a valid --out still runs baseline -> edit -> re-run -> compare -> restore and exits 0;
   existing behaviour is preserved and existing evaluate/tune tests stay green.
3. A simulated hard kill (SIGKILL) at any point after the edit leaves the CSV byte-identical to the pre-run
   state, or a deterministic, documented repair path restores it exactly.
4. The full verification command used in AH-0MVBNLM2V008XC8T (including the negative probe) completes
   without hanging; the CLI help/docs mention the new validation.
5. Unit tests cover the writeability probe, the journal/restore under simulated kill, and the CLI exit
   codes; run under the project test policy (test skill).

## Context and references
- scripts/evaluate.mjs: main(), executeTune(), applyCsvEditFile(), restoreCsvFile()
- Related work items: AH-0MVBNITA0005VQGN (--tune CLI), AH-0MVBNISWE009QFBL (CSV edit guaranteed restore),
  AH-0MVBNLM2V008XC8T (end-to-end tune-loop verification, where this was observed)
- Observed in session 2026-10-21T12-15-12-077Z (finding #2 of the session-time analysis)
- discovered-from: analysis session of 2026-10-21
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVBNITA0005VQGN** – --tune CLI: baseline, edit, re-run and compare (completed)
- **AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715** – Automate the balance-tuning loop: baseline, single-edit, re-run and diff (completed)
- **AH-0MUE2MGM0001XEH9** – CSV seed data files (enemy-configs.csv, ship-config.csv) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, active, activity, add, agent (+176 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: active, activity, add, agent, also (+156 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: active, add, agent, also, balance (+155 more)

## Goal (tracer-bullet vertical slice)

Ship the first end-to-end music slice: the menu/attract ambient track ("Star Drift", Lydian) played through the existing shared AudioContext, driven by a minimal music state machine, with the autoplay/gesture guard and an independent music volume control.

This slice cuts through every layer — baked asset, playback facade, state machine, scene wiring, settings, tests, docs — so later slices extend a proven path rather than a horizontal layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The menu/attract state plays the baked "Star Drift" Lydian ambient stem as a seamless loop.
- [ ] Music starts only after a user gesture, honouring the AudioContext resume discipline (GDD 7.3), and reuses the single shared AudioContext owned by the playback provider.
- [ ] Music volume and mute are independent of SFX and persisted in the settings record.
- [ ] The state machine enters and leaves the menu/attract state only at a bar boundary of the shared beat clock.
- [ ] Unit tests cover stem looping, the gesture guard, independent volume routing and the menu/attract transition; all playback degrades to a safe no-op without an AudioContext.

- [ ] Covers parent AC5: **Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.

## Minimal implementation

data.description:
# Intake brief — Permanent Force Field should regenerate its reflect budget (AH-0MVNX40F2005CM8P)

## Headline

A hold-full (permanent) Force Field spends its 3–10 reflections once and then
sits dim and inert for the rest of the run, so the permanent reward stops being
a reward. Give the bubble a level-resolved recharge so a spent reflection
returns over time — mirroring the Thorn Field recharge
(AH-0MVJ8YKR70096C6T) — with the dim bubble brightening back to the active look
as reflections return, driven once from the shared registry tick so the game
and every gym behave identically.

## Problem statement

`EffectsRegistry.tryConsumeForceFieldReflect()` decrements `_forceFieldRemaining`
and nothing ever puts a reflection back: `_forceFieldRemaining` is only ever
assigned on collection (`applyCollect`), cleared on window expiry
(`_expireTimedEffect`) and cleared by `reset()`. A **permanent** (hold-full)
field therefore starts at its level-resolved budget and, once spent, stays at
zero for the whole run. After AH-0MVRDMG0N000Y03Z made the spent bubble **dim
rather than vanish**, that permanent reward now visibly advertises "up but
inert" for the remainder of the run.

The Thorn Field solved the same "permanent reward goes inert" problem with a
level-resolved recharge clock advanced from the shared `EffectsRegistry.tick`
(AH-0MVJ8YKR70096C6T). The Force Field has no equivalent.

## Users

- **Players who take the hold-full "Force Field" reward** — they paid a full
  hold for a permanent upgrade and expect it to keep earning reflections.

User stories:

- As a player with a permanent Force Field, I want spent reflections to come
  back over time, so my hold-full reward keeps defending me instead of going
  quiet after three bounces.
- As a player, I want to see when the next reflection is due, so the dim bubble
  does not read as broken.
- As a player, I want the bubble to visibly return to its active look when a
  reflection comes back, so I can tell "recharging" from "dead".
- As a maintainer, I want the recharge to live once in the shared
  `EffectsRegistry` tick, so the game and every gym refill identically
  (gym↔game parity, AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Recharge clock.** A new level-resolved interval puts one spent reflection
  back: `EffectsRegistry` exposes `forceFieldRechargeTime()`,
  `forceFieldRechargeRemaining()` and `forceFieldMaxReflects()` (the resolved
  `forceFieldReflects` budget), advanced **only** from the shared
  `EffectsRegistry.tick(dt)` (the single call site every scene already uses).
  One reflection returns per elapsed interval, a long frame returns exactly as
  many reflections as the elapsed time warrants (remainder carried, no
  banking), and the budget never exceeds `forceFieldMaxReflects()`.
- **Level axis.** A new `forceFieldRecharge` variable in
  `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.force_field` (descending linear-clamped interval, whole
  seconds) plus the derived, monotonic non-decreasing rate axis
  `forceFieldRechargeRate = 1 / interval`, mirroring `thornsRecharge` /
  `thornsRechargeRate`. Draft tuning: **12 s at level 0 → 5 s floor, −1 s per
  level** (see Open Question 1).
- **Scope.** Recharge runs while a Force Field is active — for the whole run on
  a permanent (hold-full) grant, and while its window is still open on a field
  pickup — up to the level-resolved budget. A spent budget on an inactive field
  never resurrects (window expiry and `reset()` clear the clock, exactly like
  the Thorn Field).
- **Visual follow-through.** The bubble returns from the AH-0MVRDMG0N000Y03Z
  spent-dim look to the active look as soon as `forceFieldRemaining() > 0`, and
  dims again when it is spent — through the existing shared
  `drawForceFieldBubble` gate, with no per-scene branch.
- **HUD.** The `Force Field ×N` row gains the `next in Ns` recharge countdown
  while a reflection is owed (extending `HUD._powerUpRecharge`, the same path
  the Thorn Field and permanent Orbital Strike use) and otherwise renders as it
  does today.
- **Tests.** Unit tests cover: one reflection per interval; cap at the
  level-resolved budget; frame-rate independence (many small ticks vs one long
  tick); no recharge while the window is inactive (temporary expiry clears the
  clock); a permanent field recharging for the whole run; a stronger level
  recharging faster; `reset()` clearing the clock; `forceFieldRechargeRemaining()`
  reported only while a reflection is owed; and the dim → active bubble
  transition driven by the refilled budget.
- **Gym↔game parity.** The registry tick remains the only recharge driver, and
  the existing parity suites (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`,
  `powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`, `GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` plus the
  `GymPowerUpLeveling` readout) cover the new axis without a second code path.
- **Docs.** The GDD `force_field` row (§4.2) and the power-up level-variable
  table (§ around line 1205) describe the recharge; the power-up description
  copy in `src/powerups/types.ts` (surfaced in the hold-full choice/help)
  mentions the budget returning over time. All related documentation is
  updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any
  relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **One shared code path.** No scene-specific recharge timers; the clock lives
  in `EffectsRegistry` and advances only from `tick`, which `CombatScene` /
  `CombatCoreScene` already call for both `PlayScene` and every gym.
- **Additive level axis only.** Do not change existing `forceFieldDuration` /
  `forceFieldReflects` base/cap values or behaviour; the new axis is additive
  and monotonic (`POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` is iterated by completeness and
  monotonicity tests, so it must be registered in catalogue order).
- **No new assets, cues or textures.** The recharge is a timer plus the
  existing two-state bubble look; no new sound, no new VFX module.
- **Balance guardrail.** Recharge must stay slow enough that a field is never
  permanent immunity — the resolved budget cap plus a multi-second interval is
  the bound, exactly as for the Thorn Field.
- **CHANGELOG.md is out of scope** (ship-skill release pipeline owns it).

## Existing state

- `EffectsRegistry` (`src/powerups/effects.ts`): `_forceFieldRemaining` (declared
  `:379`, set from `stats.forceFieldReflects` in `applyCollect` `:595`, cleared
  by `reset()` `:788` and by `_expireTimedEffect` `:787`, decremented in
  `tryConsumeForceFieldReflect` `:922`). Accessors `isForceFieldActive()` `:855`,
  `forceFieldRemaining()` `:864`, `forceFieldRadius()` `:872`.
- `tick(dt)` `:721` is the single shared advance path; it already drives
  `_levelStore.tickRecharge(dt)` and `_advanceThornsRecharge(dt)` — the direct
  precedent for a `_advanceForceFieldRecharge(dt)` call placed alongside it.
- Thorn Field recharge model to mirror: `_thornsRechargeTimer` `:405`,
  clock start in `tryConsumeThornsRam()` `:1124`, `thornsMaxAbsorbs()` `:1140`,
  `thornsRechargeTime()` `:1156`, `thornsRechargeRemaining()` `:1169`,
  `_advanceThornsRecharge(dt)` `:1182` (carries the remainder in a `while` loop,
  clears the clock on a full budget or an inactive window).
- Level model (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`): `force_field` specs at `:753`
  (`forceFieldDuration` 8 → 18 s, `forceFieldReflects` 3 → 10);
  `thornsRecharge` spec at `:907` (12 → 5 s, `k = -1`, `discrete: true`) with the
  derived `thornsRechargeRate` computed in the resolver (`:1214`) — the template
  for the new axis and its derived rate.
- Visual: `drawForceFieldBubble` (`src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts:304`)
  already gates on `isForceFieldActive()` and switches to the spent alphas when
  `registry.forceFieldRemaining() <= 0` (`:354`), so a refilled budget restores
  the active look with no visual change — the AC only needs a test pinning it.
- HUD (`src/ui/HUD.ts`): `_powerUpStacks` returns `forceFieldRemaining()` (`:549`);
  `_powerUpRecharge` (`:575`) handles `thorns` and `strike` only — the Force
  Field case is the gap.
- Power-up copy (`src/powerups/types.ts:233`): "the field returns a limited
  number of shots before it stops reflecting" — no mention of a returning
  budget.

## Desired change

1. Add the `forceFieldRecharge` level axis (interval, descending) and derive
   `forceFieldRechargeRate`, registered in `POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` in
   catalogue order right after `forceFieldReflects`.
2. Add the Force Field recharge clock to `EffectsRegistry`: start it on the
   first spent reflection (keeping a running countdown, never banking time),
   advance it from `tick`, cap the refill at the resolved budget, clear it when
   the field is inactive or the budget is full, and clear it in `reset()`.
3. Surface `forceFieldMaxReflects()`, `forceFieldRechargeTime()` and
   `forceFieldRechargeRemaining()` for the HUD, tests and any future help copy.
4. Add the `force_field` case to `HUD._powerUpRecharge` so the row shows
   `next in Ns` while a reflection is owed.
5. Update the power-up description copy and the two GDD sections.
6. Tests as listed in the ACs, including the dim → active bubble transition.

**Key Files:**

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — Add the `forceFieldRecharge` variable, its `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.force_field` entry (12 s → 5 s, `k = -1`, `discrete: true`, with a written balance rationale), the `forceFieldRecharge`/`forceFieldRechargeRate` stat fields and the derived rate in the resolver; register the variable in `POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` after `forceFieldReflects`.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — Add `_forceFieldRechargeTimer` plus `forceFieldMaxReflects()`, `forceFieldRechargeTime()`, `forceFieldRechargeRemaining()` and `_advanceForceFieldRecharge(dt)`; start the clock in `tryConsumeForceFieldReflect()`; call the advance from `tick()` beside `_advanceThornsRecharge`; clear the clock in `_expireTimedEffect` (force_field branch) and `reset()`.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — Extend `_powerUpRecharge` with the `force_field` case mapping `forceFieldRechargeRemaining()` to the existing `next in Ns` label; update the doc comment that says only the Thorn Field recharges.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — Update the `force_field` `description` copy so the hold-full choice/help states the budget returns over time.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` — No behaviour change expected; confirm (and comment) that the spent-dim gate reads the live `forceFieldRemaining()` so a refill restores the active look.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Update the §4.2 `force_field` row and the power-up level-variable table row to describe the recharge and its draft tuning.
- `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` — Recharge unit tests (timing, cap, frame-rate independence, inactive-window clearing, permanent run-long recharge, stronger level, `reset()`, countdown reporting).
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts` — Axis tests: descending whole-second interval 12 → 5, derived rate `1 / interval` non-decreasing, existing Force Field axes unchanged.
- `src/ui/HUD.test.ts` — `next in Ns` countdown appears for a recharging Force Field and disappears when the budget is full.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.test.ts` — Pin the spent-dim → active bubble transition when the budget is refilled by the shared tick.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` and `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` / `powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts` — Extend the existing parity sweeps so the recharge is observed identically in the game and the gyms.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (recharge granularity).** One reflection returns per interval
  with the remainder carried (Thorn Field semantics), and the clock starts on
  the first spend rather than running continuously — a field re-collected at a
  full budget has no banked time. This bounds worst-case reflect throughput to
  `budget + elapsed / interval`.
- **Assumption (no idle bonus).** Recharge only runs while the field is
  active; an expired pickup window clears the clock (matching
  AH-0MVJ8YKR70096C6T) so a re-collection never inherits partial progress.
- **Risk — permanent immunity.** A short interval on a high-level field
  (10 reflections at 5 s) approaches continuous reflection. Mitigation: the
  interval floor plus the existing budget cap, and the rationale recorded beside
  the spec entry so the numbers cannot drift silently.
- **Risk — balance drift from a new axis.** Adding `forceFieldRecharge` changes
  the level-up offer surface and the "how strong is this power-up" model.
  Mitigation: additive-only axis, monotonic contract enforced by the existing
  catalogue tests and the recorded rationale.
- **Risk — HUD noise.** A countdown that persists at a full budget would read
  as a stalled timer. Mitigation: report `undefined` when nothing is owed,
  exactly like the Thorn Field.
- **Scope-creep guardrail.** A graduated (per-reflection brightness) bubble
  scale, a Force Field recharge sound or a per-level recharge VFX are **out of
  scope** — the AC needs only the binary spent/active look returning. Record
  such ideas as separate work items rather than widening this one.
- **Assumption (docs only).** No CHANGELOG entry is authored here; the release
  pipeline owns it.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14** — More forcefield feedback (parent; Q1 = dim when
  spent). Explicitly deferred regeneration to this item.
- **AH-0MVRDMG0N000Y03Z** — Force Field bubble: permanent persistence +
  spent-dim (the dim state this item has to undo on refill).
- **AH-0MVJ8YKR70096C6T** — What does Field of Thorns do? The recharge
  precedent (level axis + shared-tick clock + HUD countdown) this item mirrors.

# Fail fast on unwritable --out and invalid tune CSV

## Goal (user story)
As a developer running tune-loop verification I want `--tune` to validate `--out` (and the
balance CSV path) before anything expensive starts, so an invalid path fails in seconds with
an actionable message instead of running both sweeps first and then hanging or dying.

## Problem
`scripts/evaluate.mjs` only touches the output directory after both batches have run:
`executeTune()` calls `mkdirSync(options.outputDir, {recursive: true})` *after* the candidate
sweep (line ~394) and `main()` does the same for the non-tune path (line ~441). The 2026-10-21
negative probe (`--out /proc/nope/x`, 2 games x 200 ticks) therefore ran both sweeps and then
stalled for 166.6 minutes before an external SIGKILL (parent item AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B).

## Expected behaviour
- `node scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune --set enemy-configs.csv boss.health=7 --games 2 --ticks 200 --out <unwritable>`
  exits non-zero in well under two seconds, printing a single clear diagnostic on stderr.
- The probe runs **before** `loadCore()` (no Vite SSR boot) and before any `--tune` sweep.
- The `--tune` CSV target (`src/data/<tuneFile>`) is validated up-front too: a missing or
  unreadable CSV fails fast with its own message instead of failing after a baseline sweep.

## Implementation sketch (smallest end-to-end slice)
1. Add an exported, unit-testable probe to `scripts/evaluate.mjs`, e.g.
   `ensureWritableOutputDir(dir)` → `{ok: true}` | `{ok: false, code, message}`:
   `mkdirSync(dir, {recursive: true})`, then write + `fsync` + unlink a sentinel file
   (`.evaluate-write-probe-<pid>`) so an unwritable-but-existing directory (`EACCES`) is
   caught, not just a non-creatable one (`ENOTDIR`, `EROFS`).
2. Export a matching `assertTuneInputs(csvPath)` (`readFileSync` probe) for the `--tune` CSV.
3. In `main()`, call the probes immediately after `parseEvaluateArgs`/`--help` handling and
   **before** `loadCore()`; on failure write `output directory not writable: <dir> (<code>)`
   (and the CSV equivalent) to stderr and return a non-zero exit code (2 — same class as the
   existing usage-error exit, documented in `EVALUATE_USAGE`).
4. Keep the late `mkdirSync` calls as a cheap idempotent safety net; do not duplicate the
   validity logic.
5. Update `EVALUATE_USAGE` and `docs/BALANCING.md` (§Tuning loop → "Guards and guarantees")
   with the fail-fast validation, and extend the doc guard
   (`src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`) to assert the new statements.

## Key Files
- scripts/evaluate.mjs
- scripts/evaluate-failfast.test.ts
- scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts
- docs/BALANCING.md
- src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The repro command fails fast (< 2 s) with a clear "output directory not writable" diagnostic and a non-zero exit, demonstrated after the fix (timings quoted in a work-item comment).
2. The writeability probe and CSV-path validation run before loadCore() and before any baseline or candidate sweep, proven by a test that observes no SSR boot on the failure path.
3. An unwritable-but-existing directory (EACCES) and a non-directory path (ENOTDIR) both fail fast, and the --tune CSV path is validated before the baseline sweep.
4. --tune with a valid --out still runs baseline -> edit -> re-run -> compare -> restore and exits 0; existing behaviour is preserved and existing evaluate/tune tests stay green.
5. CLI help (EVALUATE_USAGE) and docs/BALANCING.md mention the new validation, and the docs-guard test asserts it.
6. Unit tests cover the writeability probe and the CLI exit codes for each failure path, run under the project test policy (test skill).

# Journal the tune CSV edit so a hard kill cannot leave it dirty

## Goal (user story)
As a developer I want the tune/edit cycle crash-safe, so that even an external SIGKILL, OOM or
timeout kill of the CLI never leaves `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` edited in the worktree — or,
if it does, the very next invocation (or a documented one-line command) restores it exactly.

## Problem
`executeTune()` applies the edit through `applyCsvEditFile()` and restores it in a `finally`
via `restoreCsvFile()` using the in-memory `attempt.originalText`. A SIGKILL runs no `finally`,
so the edited CSV survives the process (observed on 2026-10-21 immediately after the exit-137
kill, parent item AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B).

## Expected behaviour
- Before the first edited byte is written, a small journal (target path + original bytes) is
  persisted beside the CSV and fsynced.
- The journal is git-ignored, so a crashed run never shows up as a worktree change.
- After a successful restore (or with `--keep-edit`) the journal is removed.
- Any subsequent `scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune` invocation that finds a stale journal first
  reconciles it (restores the original bytes, removes the journal, prints a warning) and then
  proceeds — so no manual step is needed in the normal case.
- A documented manual repair path exists for the case where the CSV must be restored without
  running the CLI again.

## Implementation sketch (smallest end-to-end slice)
1. New module `scripts/csvEditJournal.mjs`:
   `writeJournal(csvPath, originalBytes)` — write `<csvPath>.tune-journal` (JSON: csvPath,
   base64 original, pid, ISO timestamp) to a temp name, `fsync`, `rename` (atomic);
   `readJournal(path)`; `clearJournal(path)`; `reconcileJournal(path)` — restore original
   bytes when the journal exists, then delete it, returning `{action: 'restored'|'none'}`.
2. Wire into `executeTune()`: write the journal before `applyCsvEditFile`'s write, and clear
   it inside the existing `finally` after `restoreCsvFile()` resolves.
3. `main()` reconciles a stale journal for the `--tune` target before validation proceeds.
4. Add the journal pattern to `.gitignore` (e.g. `src/data/*.tune-journal`).
5. Document the guarantee + repair commands in `docs/BALANCING.md` (§Tuning loop →
   "Guards and guarantees"), and assert it in `src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`.

## Key Files
- scripts/evaluate.mjs
- scripts/csvEditJournal.mjs
- scripts/evaluate-failfast.test.ts
- scripts/csvEdit-shell.test.ts
- src/utils/csvEdit.ts
- docs/BALANCING.md
- scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A simulated hard kill (SIGKILL) after the edit leaves a journal; the next invocation restores the CSV byte-identical to the pre-run state, verified by a test that kills a child process and compares bytes.
2. The journal is written (fsynced, atomically renamed) beside the CSV before the edited bytes are written, and is removed after a successful restore or when --keep-edit is used.
3. The journal path is git-ignored so a crashed run leaves no worktree change, asserted by a .gitignore guard test.
4. A deterministic, documented repair path restores the CSV exactly, documented in docs/BALANCING.md together with the journal file name.
5. Unit tests cover the journal write, restore-from-journal and stale-journal reconciliation, run under the project test policy (test skill).
6. Existing tune behaviour is preserved: --tune with a valid --out still runs baseline -> edit -> re-run -> compare -> restore, exits 0, and existing evaluate/tune tests stay green.

# Per-run progress output and opt-in sweep watchdog

## Goal (user story)
As a developer (or an agent) running a long tune sweep I want visible per-run progress and an
opt-in bounded-runtime guard, so an abnormal run can never stall silently for hours and so a
timeout aborts cleanly with the CSV already restored.

## Problem
`--tune` prints nothing between start and the final summary: `executeTune()` runs two
`runBalanceBatch()` sweeps with no output. When the 2026-10-21 negative probe stalled, the only
signal was a silent process for 166.6 minutes until an external SIGKILL (parent item
AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B). After slice 2 the known hang is gone, but a future stall in the sweep
itself (configuration-driven blow-up, non-determinism guard loop, I/O stall) would again be
invisible.

## Expected behaviour
- Every `--tune` run writes one progress line per completed game to **stderr**:
  `[tune] baseline 1/2 seed=1 policy=competent`, then `[tune] candidate 2/2 …`, then the phase
  transitions (edit applied, comparing, restoring). Stdout stays byte-identical to today so
  artifact/print parity and determinism are preserved.
- `--watchdog <seconds>` (default `0` = off) arms a bounded-runtime guard: on expiry the run
  prints a diagnostic naming the phase and the elapsed time, restores the CSV (journal from
  slice 3 + synchronous restore), and exits with a distinct code (124) rather than leaving a
  killed-but-dirty worktree.
- `--help` and `docs/BALANCING.md` document both.

## Implementation sketch (smallest end-to-end slice)
1. Reuse the existing per-run hook instead of adding a second mechanism: `runBatch` already
   accepts `config.onRun` (`src/ai/eval/engine.ts`), but `runBalanceBatch()` in
   `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` does not expose it (and `CliOptions.telemetrySink` is ignored there).
   Add an optional second parameter `runBalanceBatch(options, hooks?: {onRun?})` that forwards
   `onRun`; keep the existing signature/behaviour when `hooks` is omitted.
2. In `executeTune()`, pass an `onRun` that writes the progress line to `io.err` (count games
   against `sweep.seeds.length * policies.length`) — no divergent copy of the sweep logic.
3. Add `--watchdog <seconds>` parsing to `parseEvaluateArgs` (validated: finite, >= 0;
   non-numeric → usage error exit 2), arm a timer in `executeTune()` and clear it in the
   existing `finally`; on expiry: diagnostic + `restoreCsvFile` + `process.exitCode = 124`
   (use `exitCode`, not `exit()`, so pending stderr drains and the pipe cannot mask the exit).
4. Docs: `docs/BALANCING.md` tune flags table + "Guards and guarantees"; assert in
   `src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`.

## Risky assumptions
- A watchdog timer inside a synchronous sweep cannot interrupt a *blocking* synchronous call —
  it only fires between runs. Recorded as an accepted limitation: the guard catches stalls that
  yield to the event loop (the observed case is caught by slice 2's fail-fast path instead), and
  the progress lines remain the primary signal for a truly blocking stall. Document this
  limitation in `docs/BALANCING.md`.

## Key Files
- scripts/evaluate.mjs
- src/ai/eval/cli.ts
- src/ai/eval/engine.ts
- src/ai/eval/cli.test.ts
- scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts
- docs/BALANCING.md

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Every --tune run emits per-run progress lines on stderr (never stdout), covered by a unit test that captures both streams.
2. An opt-in bounded-runtime watchdog (--watchdog <seconds>) aborts the sweep with a clear diagnostic naming the stalled phase, restores the CSV, and exits with a distinct non-zero code, covered by a test.
3. The full verification command used in AH-0MVBNLM2V008XC8T (including the negative probe) completes without hanging, with elapsed times recorded in a work-item comment.
4. Progress wiring reuses the shared runBatch onRun hook through runBalanceBatch (no divergent sweep copy in the shell), covered by cli.test.ts.
5. Artifact/print parity is preserved: stdout and the four tune artifacts are byte-identical to the pre-change output for the same seed/options (determinism tests stay green).
6. --help and docs/BALANCING.md document --watchdog, its default (off), its exit code, and the accepted limitation that a blocking synchronous stall cannot be interrupted, asserted by the docs guard.

## Context

Part of **Mini-Boss rewards become valuable (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD)**. The
paired implementation item for "Test the mini-boss wheel overlay and spin
behaviour": this item makes those tests green.

## Summary

New launcher-agnostic wheel overlay scene `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts`
mirroring `MineralChoiceScene`'s overlay pattern (pause, single optional
result callback, demo auto-select contract). The scene receives the owned-kind
wedges and a resolved outcome from the launcher; it only animates and reports,
never computes probabilities.

## Design

- Registered in `src/core/gameConfig.ts` so `scene.launch('MiniBossWheelScene',
  …)` works everywhere.
- Payload: `wedges` (one per owned permanent kind + bonus wedge, each carrying
  the code-drawn icon + display name), `outcome` (target wedge index + extra
  gained wedges for multi-upgrade spins), optional `onResult` callback
  (mirrors `MineralChoiceScene.onSelect`), and optional `autoSpinMs`
  (demo mode: after `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`) / `fireSchedule` (reduced-
  volume ghost fire while paused, reusing the shared hold-full metronome).
- Spin: pointer click or any keyboard key starts a fast-start, ease-out
  rotation (≈2.2 s total, at most one overshoot revolution, duration exported
  as a constant) that stops on the target wedge; the landed wedge is
  highlighted; the result callback fires exactly once; a later spin is a
  no-op.
- **Multi-upgrade reveal (producer answer Q2):** when the outcome grants 2–3
  kinds, the landing wedge renders **all** the gained kinds' icons inside that
  one wedge ("all icons present") — the other gained kinds are not lit up on
  separate wedges — so the complete result is legible at the pointer.
- Tension over predictability: the wedge list order and the target angle are
  hidden from the player until the spin stops (outcome resolved by the
  launcher from the run-seeded RNG before launch).
- Code-first visuals only (`drawPowerUpIcon` / `drawWeaponIcon`); no external
  art assets.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts` (new)
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` (register the scene)
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` (reused unchanged)
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` (pattern reference)
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` (outcome resolution, consumed unchanged)
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MiniBossWheelScene.test.ts` (paired test item)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: "Test the mini-boss wheel overlay and spin behaviour" and "Pure
  wheel slot distribution and outcome resolver"
- Blocks: "Rework PlayScene mini-boss reward to the wheel", "Prove gym↔game
  parity for the mini-boss wheel reward"
- Related: parent AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD (AC1, AC2, AC6)

## Acceptance Criteria

- A wheel overlay scene exists (`src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts`), registered in `src/core/gameConfig.ts`, presenting **one wedge per owned permanent kind** across the shared six-slot pool (power-up kinds **and** weapon drops) **plus a single bonus wedge**, drawn with the existing code-drawn icons; the upgrade-or-unlock menu is never shown through this surface.
- Play is paused exactly like the hold-full choice while the overlay is open, and the overlay closes and gameplay resumes when the result callback completes.
- Spinning is **player-initiated** (click/keyboard): the wheel animation starts fast and eases out (≈2.2 s total, at most one overshoot revolution, duration exported as a constant), the outcome is not predictable until it stops, and the landed wedge is highlighted and applied exactly once.
- A **multi-upgrade outcome's landing wedge shows all the gained kinds' icons** in that one wedge (producer answer Q2 — "the wedge with the multi-results has all icons present"), with no separate highlights on other wedges, and the whole outcome applied exactly once.
- Level-saturated kinds are **not** filtered out of the draws (producer answer Q1 = Option A): the wheel matches the hold-full choice and a spin always increments levels.
- The scene is launcher-agnostic: it receives the wedges and the resolved outcome, exposes a **single optional result callback** (mirroring `MineralChoiceScene.onSelect`), never computes probabilities itself, and never reaches into a launcher by key.
- Demo mode auto-spins after `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` so the attract bot never stalls; normal play waits for input.
- The paired test item's tests pass and the changed-scope gate is green.

resolved outcome exactly once through the shared reward machinery, falls back
to the hold-full-style three-option choice when nothing permanent is owned,
and keeps the demo auto-spin. The unlock machinery is already removed (parent
AC5, sibling item).

## Design

- Open: build the owned-kind snapshot once from
  `resolvePlayerSlotState(this.player).ownedIds`
  (power-up kinds and weapon drops; permanent view). When empty →
  **fallback**: open the shared `MineralChoiceScene` with the hold-full-style
  three options (`createRandomChoiceStrategy` / `chooseOptions`), applied
  permanently — a mini-boss always pays out (AC4).
- When populated: resolve the wheel outcome once from the run-seeded RNG
  (`drawWheelOutcome`/`miniBossWheel`) and launch `MiniBossWheelScene` with the
  wedges, the outcome and a single result callback. Pause exactly like the
  hold-full choice; pass the frozen fire schedule for the reduced-volume ghost
  fire; rebase the beat clock on resume.
- Select/result: apply the outcome once via `applyWheelOutcome`
  (shared reward seam), close the overlay, resume play, reset the open flag —
  a repeated select is a no-op.
- Demo mode: pass `autoSpinMs: BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` so the attract bot
  auto-spins from the run-seeded RNG and never stalls.
- Test getters (`getMiniBossRewardOptions`, `isMiniBossRewardOpen`) preserved
  or re-homed so the wheel-flow tests keep a stable surface.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (rework `openMiniBossReward` /
  `selectMiniBossReward`; drop unlock state)
- `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts` (launched overlay)
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` (outcome resolution + application)
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` (`resolvePlayerSlotState` — owned kinds)
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` (`chooseOptions` for the fallback)
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`
  (paired test item)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: "Test the PlayScene wheel reward flow and empty-owned fallback",
  "Launcher-agnostic mini-boss wheel overlay scene", "Pure wheel slot
  distribution and outcome resolver" and "Remove the weapon-unlock reward
  feature and bump checkpoint version"
- Blocks: "Prove gym↔game parity for the mini-boss wheel reward",
  "Document the wheel reward and unlock removal"
- Related: parent AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD (AC1, AC2, AC4, AC6)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Defeating a mini-boss opens the **wheel overlay** with one wedge per owned permanent kind across the shared six-slot pool (power-up kinds and weapon drops) plus a single bonus wedge; the multi-option upgrade-or-unlock choice is gone and play is paused exactly like the hold-full choice.
- The spin is player-initiated, and the resolved outcome (from the 100-slot distribution via the shared resolver) is applied **exactly once** through the shared reward machinery — a repeated select/spin is a no-op.
- **Empty-owned fallback:** when the player owns no permanent kinds at a mini-boss defeat, the wheel is not shown and the existing hold-full-style three-option choice is offered instead, so a mini-boss always pays out.
- Demo mode auto-spins after `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` from the run-seeded RNG so the attract bot never stalls.
- No `Math.random()` or unlock-state remains in the reward path; the wheel flow consumes the shared modules only.
- The paired test item's tests pass and the changed-scope gate is green.

# Seam-aware threat and hazard prediction

Parent: "Bot should be aware of screen wrap around" (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG) — AC3.

## Goal (user story)

As a **player**, I want the demo bot to dodge a shot that is about to arrive
across the seam, so it survives what any human sees coming — now that wrap-aware
enemies fire across seams (AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8).

## Context

Threat prediction is raw Euclidean:

- `predictIncomingFire` and `classifyShot` (`src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts`) —
  relative position/velocity of the shot vs. the player, closest approach on the
  raw line; the fire-tell estimate is a straight line from the enemy to the
  player's raw position;
- the competent `closestApproach` solve
  (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`) used by `evaluateDirection` for
  hazards and incoming fire, and by `hazardThreatensPlayer` / the engage kiting
  gate;
- the legacy path-crossing checks in `src/ai/botDecision.ts`
  (`evaluateVector`'s bullet and fire-tell solves);
- `hazardVelocity` (`src/ai/framework/hazardVelocity.ts`) already clamps
  spurious position jumps (`HAZARD_MAX_ESTIMATED_SPEED = 900`) to filter
  wrap-around/respawn teleports.

Consequence: a bullet that will arrive from the opposite edge is predicted on a
line that starts ~900 px away in the wrong direction, so the bot stands still
and dies to it.

## Scope

1. Wrap the *relative* geometry of the prediction: the shot-to-player separation
   is the shortest wrapped delta (per axis), so closest approach and time-to-
   closest are computed on the torus. Where wrapping changes the problem, the
   predicted approach is taken along the wrapped route.
2. Compute the wrapped route for both in-flight bullets and fire-tell estimates
   (`predictIncomingFire`'s `assumedBulletSpeed` line) so a tell that will fire
   across the seam is classified as threatening.
3. Run the competent `closestApproach` (hazards and incoming fire) and the legacy
   path-crossing solves on the wrapped deltas, sharing one implementation.
4. Re-verify `hazardVelocity`'s clamp: with positions modelled on the torus the
   tracker must still clamp only true teleports/respawns and must not swallow a
   legitimate seam re-entry (which is a real ~width-sized jump in raw
   coordinates). Prefer wrapping the *delta* used to estimate velocity over
   raising the clamp; if a change is needed, cover it with tests proving a seam
   crossing yields the hazard's true velocity and a respawn still yields zero/its
   previous estimate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Seam-aware threat and hazard prediction: `predictIncomingFire` runs on the wrapped torus.
2. `predictIncomingFire` (`src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts`), the competent
   `closestApproach` solves and the legacy path-crossing checks
   (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`, `src/ai/botDecision.ts`) operate on
   the wrapped torus, using the shared wrap-geometry primitives.
3. A seam-crossing shot is classified as threatening: a test places an enemy
   bullet just outside one edge travelling inward so its wrapped path crosses the
   player, and asserts `threatens === true` and a small `closestDistance` /
   `timeToClosest` — a raw-line-only view would miss it (assert the raw view
   would give a large distance in the same test as a comment/assertion).
4. A shot on the player's own side of the seam is classified exactly as before
   today's behaviour (regression assertion on distance/time/threatens).
5. The `hazardVelocity` tracker's wrap-jump clamp is re-verified and tested: a
   hazard that crosses a seam between decision ticks yields its true (small)
   velocity rather than a clamped/absurd one, and a genuine respawn/teleport is
   still clamped — so the tracker never double-compensates under the torus model.
6. `evaluateDirection` rejects an unsafe bearing when a seam-crossing shot is
   predicted to intersect it, and `hazardThreatensPlayer` reports a seam-crossing
   hazard as threatening.
7. The changed-scope test gate passes via `/skill:test` (build → test → commit
   order) with tests written first.
##

# Wrap docs and full validation sweep

Parent: "Bot should be aware of screen wrap around" (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG) — AC6.

## Goal (user story)

As a **developer**, I want the bot framework and evaluation docs to describe the
wrap-aware (torus) model, and a wrap-scenario validation sweep that proves the
human-like feel is preserved, so the next person changing bot behaviour knows the
model and can trust the suite.

## Context

The decision layer's documented model will have changed substantially: edges are
no longer walls, geometry is wrapped, `wallMargin` is gone and eval is
wrap-parity. `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` and `docs/EVALUATION.md` currently describe
the pre-wrap model, and repo docs are asserted by tests
(`src/ai/framework/botFrameworkDocs.test.ts`,
`src/ai/framework/competent/competentBotDocs.test.ts`,
`src/ai/eval/evaluationDocs.test.ts`, `src/wrapAwareDocs.test.ts`).

## Scope

1. `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — document the single wrap-aware model: the shared
   wrap-geometry helpers and where they live, wrapped steering/aim/nearest/
   threat prediction, the near-tie hysteresis, the retired `wallMargin`, and the
   preserved human-like governor (reaction cadence, W/A/D, thrust feel).
2. `docs/EVALUATION.md` — document eval wrap parity (wrapped bullets, seam-aware
   hostile aim) and what it means for score comparison.
3. Wrap-scenario tests that exercise the whole stack end-to-end (not just unit
   level): a competent-bot integration scenario where the shortest route to a
   target is across a seam (bot crosses and reaches it), and a survival scenario
   where a seam-arriving shot is dodged; the human-like governor's cadence/controls
   assertions stay green.
4. Full-suite validation: the changed-scope gate first, then the dev-push gate's
   full suite (never run ad hoc — always via `/skill:test`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Unit/integration tests cover wrapped steering (all four edges, raw vs.
   wrapped), seam aim, seam threat prediction, wrapped nearest-selection where raw
   and wrapped ordering differ, wall-margin retirement and eval parity — each
   traced to the child that added it, with the docs child adding the end-to-end
   scenarios rather than duplicating unit coverage.
2. The human-like governor's reaction cadence, controls and thrust feel are
   unchanged: existing steering/bot integration tests stay green, plus new wrap
   scenarios (`src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts`,
   `src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts`) that assert the bot crosses a seam
   for a nearer target and dodges a seam-arriving shot.
3. `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` and `docs/EVALUATION.md` describe the wrap-aware model
   (shared helpers, wrapped steering/aim/nearest/threat, hysteresis, retired
   `wallMargin`, eval parity), and the docs-assertion tests
   (`botFrameworkDocs.test.ts` and the eval docs tests) are updated and green.
4. The full project test suite passes via `/skill:test` with the new changes; no
   ad-hoc test invocation is used.
5. Any divergence discovered (behaviour deliberately left wrap-blind, or a gym/game
   parity caveat) is recorded in the work-item comment and, where non-obvious, a
   code comment next to the divergence.

## Key Files

- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md`.
- `src/ai/framework/botFrameworkDocs.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBotDocs.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/eval/evaluationDocs.test.ts`, `src/wrapAwareDocs.test.ts`.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by every other child of this epic (steering, aim, nearest-selection,
threat prediction, wallMargin retirement, eval parity) — it documents and
validates their combined result.
